points.description: Defines height in terms of a path from the root of the tree down to a leaf, with its length measured as the number of edges (or steps) along that path. Equivalent wording such as 'the path from the root to a leaf' earns the mark.
States that the height is the longest (maximum length) of all such root-to-leaf paths, not just any one path. Equivalent wording such as 'the maximum over all root-to-leaf paths' earns the mark.

rubric.notes: A full-mark answer defines height as the length of the longest path from the root to a leaf, using equivalent wording. Award P1 for the root-to-leaf path idea and P2 for the 'longest' (maximum) requirement. An answer that gives only a single path length without taking the longest earns 2 marks.
